# Image-container corpus

All `.gz` files are losslessly compressed test inputs, decompressed to temporary
directories by the Rust tests. Tests need no network or external parser.

`dfvfs-sources.json` pins the upstream URLs, Git blob IDs, byte lengths and
uncompressed SHA-256 hashes for split raw, VMDK and VHD images from
[dfVFS](https://github.com/log2timeline/dfvfs/tree/d365f334da42169276e2083a27f75bc2afa48ea8/test_data),
commit `d365f334da42169276e2083a27f75bc2afa48ea8`.
The accompanying [dfVFS license](../LICENSE.dfvfs) applies. The generated
containers below wrap the existing dfVFS `ext2.raw` image under that license.

`tsk-image-reference.json` records complete decoded-stream lengths and hashes.
`.decoded.gz` streams came from TSK 4.15.0's `img_cat` using its independent
raw/libvmdk/libvhdi adapters, except for the differential VHD overlay below.
The original `image.vhd` has invalid footer checksums and is deliberately
rejected. `image-differential.vhd` references that invalid parent and is also
a rejection test. Neither input was repaired to make a positive test pass.

The installed libvhdi does not honor individual sector inheritance bits in
allocated differential blocks. For `fat-differential.vhd` and
`ntfs-differential.vhd`, `tools/validate_images.py` independently applies the
specified MSB-first sector-bitmap overlay to a parent decoded by TSK. Changed
child sectors are also compared with libvhdi using an explicitly attached
parent. These two goldens are specification-based overlays, not claimed to be
unmodified TSK exports. The format reference is
[libyal's VHD specification](https://github.com/libyal/libvhdi/blob/main/documentation/Virtual%20Hard%20Disk%20(VHD)%20image%20format.asciidoc).

`qemu-generated.json` records containers generated by QEMU 2.3.0 for
`monolithicSparse`, `streamOptimized`, `twoGbMaxExtentSparse`,
`monolithicFlat` and `twoGbMaxExtentFlat`. QEMU reread each output and matched
the original raw bytes. The streamFooter fixture adds the specified
`GD_AT_END` framing around QEMU's existing grains and index; TSK/libvmdk
independently decoded it to the original raw image. These small split VMDKs
have one external extent; multiple-extent boundary behavior is covered by
explicit Rust fixtures too. VMDK parent/zero override tests construct a small
specified sparse layout with known byte patterns.

QEMU development binary: [Cloudbase's Windows build](https://cloudbase.it/qemu-img-windows/),
archive `qemu-img-win-x64-2_3_0.zip`, SHA-256
`8dc1c69d9880919cdad8c09126a016262d4a9edf48b87a1ef587914fe4177909`.
No executable or QEMU library is needed at runtime or shipped as a test fixture.

`afflib-generated.json` records AFFLIB 3.7.20 output: `native.aff` (zlib),
`plain.aff` (uncompressed), `lzma.aff`, `multi.afd/file_000.aff` through
`file_002.aff`, and `native.afm` with four 1 MiB raw members. AFFLIB's
stream API independently reread all five logical images, matching the original
raw bytes. Native AFFLIB full-media MD5/SHA-1 hashes are also checked by Rust.
`affcat`'s page-oriented mode does not correctly export AFM, so the separate
`tools/aff_stream_oracle.cpp` uses `af_read` instead.

AFFLIB source: [sshock/AFFLIBv3 v3.7.20](https://github.com/sshock/AFFLIBv3/tree/v3.7.20),
archive SHA-256
`7264d705ff53185f0847c69abdfce072779c0b907257e087a6372c7608108f65`.
Built with MSYS2 UCRT64, `autoreconf -fi`,
`./configure --disable-shared --disable-s3 --disable-qemu --disable-fuse`,
and `make -j4`. The bundled old LZMA Windows character helpers required
pointer-width cast adjustments (`unsigned int` to `size_t`) in
`lzma443/C/Common/String.h` and `String.cpp`. The container writer/reader
logic was unchanged. The external oracle is never linked into Rust.
AFFLIB output includes creation-time metadata, so regenerating containers
changes their container hashes; decoded evidence remains identical.

Optional reproduction, from the project root (add native tool DLLs to PATH):

```powershell
python tools/fetch_image_fixtures.py
python tools/generate_image_fixtures.py --qemu target/qemu-oracle/qemu-img.exe
cargo build --locked
python tools/validate_images.py --tsk target/tsk-oracle/sleuthkit-4.15.0-win32/bin/img_cat.exe --vhdi D:/Projects/autopsy/thirdparty/opencv/lib/x86_64/libvhdi.dll
python tools/validate_aff_images.py --afflib-bin target/afflib-build/AFFLIBv3-3.7.20/tools --stream-oracle target/aff_stream_oracle.exe
```

Compile the stream oracle against the AFFLIB include directory and static
library, with its OpenSSL, expat, zlib, readline and platform dependencies.
The generation/validation scripts write only development files and fixtures;
they never form part of production image parsing.
